name: Flush the DNS cache
summary: Clear the list of website addresses your PC remembers.
what: Runs the command that empties the DNS resolver cache.
benefit: Fixes sites that will not load after a server move or a DNS change.
risk: None. Addresses are looked up again.
advice: Suggested when a website will not open but others do, or after you changed DNS servers.
facts: Takes a second
Does not touch your browser history or cookies
Windows rebuilds the cache as you browse

name: Reset the network stack
summary: Put Windows networking back to a clean state.
what: Resets Winsock and the IP stack, then flushes the DNS cache. A restart finishes the reset.
benefit: Can fix a PC that has no internet, drops connections or has odd network errors after software changes.
risk: Medium. Winsock add-ons from VPN and security software are removed and may need to be reinstalled. Static IP settings may be cleared.
advice: Suggested only after simpler fixes failed. Note your static IP and VPN details first.
facts: A restore point is made first
Restart required
VPN and some security programs may need repair afterward
Does not remove Wi-Fi passwords

name: Check and repair system files
summary: Scan Windows system files and fix damaged ones.
what: Runs the System File Checker with the full scan switch. It replaces damaged protected files from a local cache.
benefit: Fixes crashes and errors caused by damaged Windows files.
risk: None. It only restores files Windows protects.
advice: Suggested when Windows crashes, features fail to open, or updates keep failing. Run the image repair first if this one cannot fix everything.
facts: Takes 10 to 20 minutes
Safe to stop, but let it finish for a full result
If it cannot repair a file, run Repair the Windows image and then run this again

name: Scan the Windows image for damage
summary: Check whether the Windows component store is damaged.
what: Runs the DISM image scan. It only reports and changes nothing.
benefit: Tells you whether a repair is needed before you run one.
advice: Suggested before the image repair. Safe to skip if you already know you need the repair.
facts: Takes 5 to 10 minutes
Read only, nothing is changed
Reports whether the image can be repaired

name: Repair the Windows image
summary: Fix the Windows component store that updates and system file repair rely on.
what: Runs the DISM restore health command. It downloads clean files from Windows Update when it needs them.
benefit: Fixes failed updates and lets system file repair work when it could not.
risk: Low. Needs an internet connection and can take a while.
advice: Suggested when system file repair says it could not fix files, or Windows Update keeps failing.
facts: Takes 10 to 30 minutes and may look stuck near 20 percent
Needs an internet connection
Run Check and repair system files afterward

name: Clean up old Windows components
summary: Remove superseded update files from the component store.
what: Runs the DISM component cleanup. It removes older versions of components that updates replaced.
benefit: Frees disk space, often a few gigabytes.
risk: Low. You can no longer uninstall the oldest installed updates.
advice: Suggested when disk space is tight. Safe to skip otherwise.
facts: Takes 5 to 15 minutes
Does not remove installed updates
Windows also does this on its own on a schedule

name: Scan the system drive for errors
summary: Check the drive for file system problems without taking it offline.
what: Runs the online scan of the system drive. It reports problems and does not repair them.
advice: Suggested if you see file errors, slowdowns or crashes. Safe to skip on a healthy PC.
facts: Read only, nothing is repaired
Takes a few minutes
If it finds problems, repair at the next restart

name: Reset Windows Update
summary: Clear the update cache and restart the update services.
what: Stops the update services, renames the SoftwareDistribution and catroot2 folders so Windows creates fresh ones, then starts the services again. Old copies are kept with an .old name.
benefit: Fixes updates that are stuck, fail to download or keep failing to install.
risk: Medium. Update history looks empty until the next scan. The services are always started again, even if a step fails.
advice: Suggested only when updates are stuck or fail repeatedly. A restart afterward helps.
facts: A restore point is made first
Old folders are kept as .old until the next reset
Services are started again even if a step fails
The next update scan takes longer

name: Reset the Microsoft Store cache
summary: Clear the Store cache without changing your apps or account.
what: Runs the Store reset tool. It clears the Store cache and opens the Store when it finishes.
benefit: Fixes a Store that will not load, download or update apps.
risk: None. Your apps and account are not changed.
advice: Suggested when the Microsoft Store is blank, slow or stuck.
facts: Takes under a minute
The Store opens by itself when it is done
Does not remove apps or sign you out

name: Optimize the system drive
summary: Let Windows retrim an SSD or defragment a hard drive.
what: Runs the drive optimizer on the system drive. Windows picks retrim for solid state drives and defragmentation for hard drives.
benefit: Keeps a hard drive from slowing down and keeps an SSD healthy.
advice: Suggested every month or two. Windows already does this on a schedule, so you can skip it.
facts: SSDs are retrimmed, never defragmented
Hard drives can take a long time
Windows runs it weekly by itself

name: Restart the Windows audio services
summary: Bring sound back in an app that is silent while Windows sounds still play.
what: Stops the Windows Audio and Windows Audio Endpoint Builder services and starts them again, the same as restarting each one in the Services window. The services are always started again, even if a step fails.
benefit: Clears a temporary audio fault where one app has no sound but system sounds still work.
risk: Low. Sound cuts out for a few seconds, and an app that was playing may need to be reopened.
advice: Suggested when an app is silent while Windows sounds still play. Check the app's volume and output device first.
facts: Takes a few seconds
Changes no setting
Microsoft lists this as a fix for app audio that fails while system sounds work

name: Restart the Bluetooth service
summary: Reconnect Bluetooth devices that keep dropping.
what: Stops the Bluetooth Support Service and starts it again, the same as restarting it in the Services window. The service is always started again, even if the stop fails.
benefit: Clears a stuck Bluetooth stack that keeps disconnecting devices.
risk: Low. Paired devices disconnect for a moment and should reconnect by themselves. A Bluetooth keyboard or mouse that does not may need to be switched off and on, so keep another way to type nearby.
advice: Suggested when Bluetooth devices keep disconnecting. If it comes back after every restart, check the adapter's power saving setting and the driver.
facts: Takes a few seconds
Changes no setting and removes no pairing
The fix does not last across a restart of the PC if the cause is a power saving setting or a driver

name: Restart Windows Explorer
summary: Bring back a taskbar, Start menu or desktop that has frozen.
what: Ends the Windows Explorer process. Windows starts it again by itself a moment later, which reloads the taskbar, Start menu and desktop without restarting the PC.
benefit: Often fixes a frozen or blank taskbar, a Start menu that will not open, or a desktop that has stopped responding.
risk: Low. Open File Explorer windows close, and a file copy that was running in one may be interrupted. Other programs are not touched.
advice: Suggested when the taskbar or Start menu is frozen. It is the first thing to try, before a restart.
facts: Takes a few seconds
Changes no setting
The taskbar and desktop icons disappear for a moment, then come back

name: Resync the clock
summary: Ask Windows to set the clock from its time source right now.
what: Starts the Windows Time service if it is stopped, then runs w32tm /resync, which tells the PC to resynchronize its clock as soon as possible and waits for it to finish.
benefit: Fixes a clock that has drifted, which can break secure websites, sign-in and Store downloads.
risk: Low. The clock may jump by the amount it was off, which can confuse a program that was timing something.
advice: Suggested when the clock is wrong or sites report a certificate or time error. Make sure Set time automatically and the time zone are right in Settings first.
facts: Takes a few seconds and needs an internet connection
Changes no setting
If the clock is wrong again after every restart, the battery on the motherboard may be dead
